paragraphs: BOOD addresses how to create useful training examples for detecting inputs outside a model’s familiar data distribution. Generating arbitrary unusual examples is not the central challenge here: the paper focuses on finding informative features just beyond the boundary of the training distribution. Such examples can help a detector learn a clearer distinction between familiar and unfamiliar inputs.

The method first learns a text-conditioned feature space from the in-distribution dataset. It selects features near a decision boundary and perturbs them across that boundary to construct out-of-distribution features. A diffusion model then converts these features into images. This connects boundary-based feature construction with outlier images that people can inspect.

The authors report greater training efficiency and improved detection on common benchmarks. On CIFAR-100, average FPR95 falls from 40.31% to 10.67%, while average AUROC rises from 90.15% to 97.42%. These results support the usefulness of deliberately constructing boundary-adjacent outliers for the evaluated detection setting.
icml-2025-bood-boundary-based-out-of-dis.tldr: BOOD creates informative outlier images by moving learned features across decision boundaries and decoding them with a diffusion model.

paragraphs: This paper investigates why particular tokens in a mathematical reasoning sequence have an outsized influence on whether the final answer is wrong. It calls these elements critical tokens. The distinction matters because a token that strongly steers a reasoning trajectory toward failure may differ from a token identified as an ordinary error in the written solution.

The authors identify critical tokens through rollout sampling, examining generated continuations to assess their influence on outcomes. They report that replacing these tokens substantially improves accuracy. To make identification practical across larger datasets, they introduce a contrastive estimation method and incorporate the resulting token-level information into direct preference optimization, producing the training approach cDPO.

Experiments on GSM8K and MATH500 use Llama-3 models with 8 billion and 70 billion parameters and Deepseek-math with 7 billion parameters. The reported results support both critical-token replacement and cDPO. The central finding is that training can benefit from distinguishing influential reasoning choices within a sequence, rather than treating every part of that sequence as equally informative.
icml-2025-critical-tokens-matter-token-l.tldr: Identifying tokens that strongly influence reasoning failures enables targeted replacements and preference training that improve mathematical reasoning.

paragraphs: The paper studies how to infer what competing players are trying to achieve from their observed strategies and actions. It considers two-player zero-sum matrix games and Markov games with entropy regularization. Recovering rewards is difficult because different reward functions can explain similar behavior, and observations may cover only part of the relevant decisions.

The authors establish conditions for identifying reward functions using quantal response equilibrium under linear assumptions. These assumptions are central to the theoretical result: the framework provides a structured setting in which behavioral observations can distinguish rewards despite the ambiguity of the inverse problem.

Building on that foundation, the proposed algorithm constructs confidence sets intended to include all plausible reward parameters. It handles static and dynamic games and can incorporate approaches such as maximum likelihood estimation. The authors provide guarantees concerning reliability and sample efficiency, alongside experiments demonstrating accurate reward recovery across several scenarios. Representing a set of plausible rewards also makes uncertainty part of the recovery procedure, rather than reducing the task immediately to a single estimate.
icml-2025-decoding-rewards-in-competitiv.tldr: A framework recovers competitive players’ reward functions under linear assumptions while using confidence sets to represent plausible alternatives.

paragraphs: Diffusion models generate images and videos through an iterative process, making generation computationally expensive. This paper investigates whether a pretrained diffusion model can produce video in one forward evaluation while retaining useful visual quality. It builds on the motivation for one-step generation, noting that existing image distillation approaches can suffer substantial quality loss.

The proposed Adversarial Post-Training method adds a training phase against real data after diffusion pretraining. The authors also modify the architecture and training procedures to improve stability and generation quality. An approximated R1 regularization objective forms part of these changes, addressing the stability concerns associated with the post-training process.

In the reported experiments, the resulting model generates two-second videos at 1280 by 720 resolution and 24 frames per second in real time, using a single forward evaluation. It also generates 1024-pixel images in one step with quality comparable to state-of-the-art methods. These findings show that the proposed post-training approach can combine substantial generation speed with competitive image quality and demonstrated video capability.
icml-2025-diffusion-adversarial-post-tra.tldr: Adversarial post-training enables a pretrained diffusion model to generate high-resolution videos in one forward evaluation.

paragraphs: Bloom filters support approximate membership tests while using little storage. Learned Bloom filters add a predictive model, called an oracle, before the conventional filtering machinery. That model consumes part of the total memory budget, so its size affects how much space remains for the accompanying filters and how compact the complete system can be.

This paper investigates using multiple smaller oracles within the same space budget. Its contribution combines the ensemble of predictors with careful optimization of their backup filters. The design therefore treats predictor memory and filter memory as parts of one allocation problem, rather than evaluating the learned component in isolation.

The authors develop and optimize versions for both mutually independent and correlated oracles. Handling these cases separately acknowledges that the relationship between predictors matters to the filter design. Experiments on three practical data analysis tasks demonstrate improved performance. The reported result is that several smaller learned components, appropriately paired with backup filters, can outperform the single-oracle structure without increasing the overall space budget.
icml-2025-ensemble-learned-bloom-filters.tldr: Multiple smaller predictors with optimized backup filters improve learned Bloom filter performance within the same memory budget.

paragraphs: HealthGPT combines medical visual comprehension and generation in a single vision-language model. The paper organizes both capabilities within an autoregressive framework, giving them a shared modeling approach. Its central challenge is adapting different kinds of knowledge about understanding and producing medical visual content to a pretrained language model.

The proposed method transfers this heterogeneous knowledge progressively. Heterogeneous low-rank adaptation, called H-LoRA, provides the adaptation mechanism, supported by a hierarchical visual perception approach and a three-stage learning strategy. Together, these components address the representation of visual information and the process by which the model acquires its combined capabilities.

The authors also introduce VL-Health, a medical dataset designed to support both comprehension and generation. This makes the training data part of the contribution alongside the model architecture and learning procedure. Experiments report strong performance and scalability on unified medical visual tasks. The stated findings support the feasibility of developing these capabilities together through progressive adaptation of a pretrained language model.
icml-2025-healthgpt-a-medical-large-visi.tldr: HealthGPT progressively adapts a pretrained language model to combine medical visual comprehension and generation.

paragraphs: Federated learning brings together training across decentralized clients, but their data can differ substantially. Differences in data distributions and class balance can weaken a shared model’s performance. Clustered federated learning addresses this by grouping clients with similar data, allowing training to reflect those groups while retaining the decentralized setting.

FedGWC proposes a way to discover these groups through client interactions. It transforms individual empirical losses using a Gaussian reward mechanism, then uses the resulting interaction information to identify homogeneous clusters. The intended outcome is a more robust and personalized model for each identified group.

The paper also introduces the Wasserstein Adjusted Score, a metric that evaluates cluster cohesion with respect to clients’ individual class distributions. This connects the assessment of clustering quality to the data differences that motivate clustering in the first place. Benchmark experiments report better cluster quality and classification accuracy than existing federated learning algorithms, supporting the usefulness of the proposed interaction-based grouping procedure.
icml-2025-interaction-aware-gaussian-wei.tldr: FedGWC uses Gaussian-weighted client interactions to form federated learning clusters with improved classification accuracy and cluster quality.

paragraphs: This paper asks how to estimate the causal effect of one particular aspect of language on a reader’s response. For example, the target might be the effect of factual inaccuracies on beliefs. Isolating that effect requires accounting for the rest of the language, because other textual differences can also relate to the outcome.

The authors introduce a formal estimation framework centered on approximating this non-focal language. Using omitted variable bias as the organizing principle, they explain how an inadequate approximation can leave relevant variables unaccounted for and bias the estimated effect. They propose measures that evaluate both the language approximation and the resulting causal estimate.

The framework also assesses sensitivity to bias along two dimensions, fidelity and overlap. Experiments with semi-synthetic and real-world data validate its ability to recover isolated effects and demonstrate the usefulness of the measures. The contribution links the quality of a text representation to the credibility of the causal conclusion drawn from it.
icml-2025-isolated-causal-effects-of-nat.tldr: A causal estimation framework measures how accounting for surrounding language affects estimates of a specific linguistic intervention.

paragraphs: Kona addresses the communication cost of privacy-preserving nearest-neighbor classification across data held by different parties. The task benefits from access to substantial high-quality data, but those records may contain sensitive information. Existing secure frameworks can require large messages to compute distances and many exchanges to select the nearest neighbors.

The framework targets these bottlenecks separately. It introduces Euclidean triples that eliminate online communication for secure squared Euclidean distance computations. It also uses a divide-and-conquer bubble protocol to reduce the number of communication rounds needed to select the k nearest neighbors. The first contribution concerns distance computation; the second concerns neighbor selection.

Across eight real-world datasets, the authors report improvements over the state-of-the-art framework ranging from 1.1 to 3121.2 times in communication size, 16.7 to 5783.2 times in communication rounds, and 1.1 to 232.6 times in runtime. These ranges describe the evaluated settings. The results show that redesigning communication within secure classification can substantially improve practical efficiency.
icml-2025-kona-an-efficient-privacy-pres.tldr: Kona accelerates privacy-preserving KNN by reducing online distance-computation communication and the rounds needed to select neighbors.

paragraphs: The classical Black–Litterman portfolio model requires investor views: forecasts about performance relative to the market and an uncertainty matrix expressing confidence in those forecasts. This paper replaces those subjective inputs with quantities learned from market data. It treats both the forecast vector and its uncertainty matrix as latent variables within one Bayesian network.

The resulting posterior estimation has a closed-form expression, which the authors connect to fast inference and stable portfolio weights. They also propose two ways to represent interactions between features and returns: shared-latent parametrization and feature-influenced views. Both formulations include classical Black–Litterman and Markowitz portfolios as special cases, connecting the proposed approach to those established models.

Experiments use 30 years of Dow-Jones data and 20 years of sector-ETF data. The authors report a 50% improvement in Sharpe ratios and a 55% reduction in turnover relative to Markowitz and index baselines. These historical results support the proposed data-driven estimation of views and uncertainty within a coherent portfolio model.
icml-2025-latent-variable-estimation-in-.tldr: A Bayesian portfolio model learns investor views and their uncertainty from market data, with improved historical risk-adjusted returns and turnover.

paragraphs: Graph contrastive learning brings positive examples together and separates negative ones, but the paper identifies a problem with the resulting representation. Highly similar samples can form small, disconnected groups within a class, while groups and isolated samples remain scattered across the broader space. Local similarity can therefore dominate without producing compact, well-separated class clusters.

The proposed method introduces fuzzy cluster boundaries through two complementary operations. Boundary construction expands the original boundaries to connect nearby local groups. Boundary contraction then draws scattered samples or groups inside the fuzzy boundary closer together. The aim is to turn fragmented local groupings into a more coherent global cluster structure.

The authors apply this mechanism to a graph auto-encoder and evaluate both downstream tasks and quantitative properties of the learned representation. They report significant improvements over current state-of-the-art graph contrastive learning models. The findings support the value of explicitly shaping broader cluster structure when local positive and negative relationships leave the representation fragmented.
icml-2025-mitigating-local-cohesion-and-.tldr: Expanding and contracting fuzzy cluster boundaries helps graph representations join fragmented local groups into more coherent clusters.

paragraphs: EquiGX addresses how to explain predictions from equivariant graph neural networks operating on three-dimensional geometric graphs. Existing graph explanation methods largely focus on two-dimensional graph structures. According to the paper, adapting those methods to sophisticated geometric networks is difficult, particularly when explanations must account for positions and the significance of geometric features.

The method extends layer-wise relevance propagation rules for spherical equivariant graph networks using the Deep Taylor decomposition framework. It decomposes a prediction score and propagates relevance backward through the network to the inputs. This provides an account of contributions through individual layers and relates the final prediction to geometric and positional information.

Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that EquiGX identifies important geometric structures and outperforms alternative explanation baselines. The reported benefit is more informative explanations for the evaluated equivariant networks. Its central contribution is an explanation procedure adapted to the network’s geometric computations, allowing relevance to be traced through operations that existing methods struggle to handle.
icml-2025-on-explaining-equivariant-grap.tldr: EquiGX traces prediction relevance through spherical equivariant graph networks to explain the influence of geometric and positional features.

paragraphs: PARM adapts a frozen language model’s generation to user preferences that involve several objectives at once. Earlier work trains a separate autoregressive reward model for each preference dimension and combines their outputs during inference. The paper identifies both the inference expense of multiple models and preference misalignment arising from their separate training.

The proposed approach trains one autoregressive reward model across all preference dimensions. Preference-Aware Bilinear Low-Rank Adaptation conditions this model on the user’s preference vector through a bilinear form. This gives the shared reward model access to the requested combination of preferences while learning how to guide generation.

Experiments report lower inference costs and better agreement with preference vectors than existing methods. The authors also demonstrate weak-to-strong guidance: a smaller PARM can guide a larger frozen language model without expensive training of that larger model. The findings support jointly modeling preference trade-offs as a way to make inference-time alignment more efficient and responsive to different users.
icml-2025-parm-multi-objective-test-time.tldr: PARM uses one preference-conditioned reward model to guide frozen language models across multiple user objectives at lower inference cost.

paragraphs: PRIME addresses regression problems in which some target values have many training examples while others have few. The paper focuses on how this imbalance shapes learned representations. Its goal is a feature space that gives underrepresented target regions better support while retaining the ordering inherent in the values being predicted.

The method introduces learnable proxies that serve as reference points for sample features. It arranges these proxies uniformly in feature space while preserving the ordinal structure of the regression targets, then aligns each sample’s representation with its corresponding proxy. This combines balanced organization with the requirement that regression values have a meaningful order.

Because alignment to proxies resembles classification, the framework also allows techniques developed for class imbalance to be used in regression. Experiments across four real-world regression benchmarks in diverse target domains report state-of-the-art performance. The results support the use of an explicitly balanced, ordered representation as a means of improving generalization, particularly for less frequently observed target regions.
icml-2025-prime-deep-imbalanced-regressi.tldr: PRIME aligns regression features with balanced, ordered learnable proxies to improve learning across unevenly represented target values.

paragraphs: Language agents make sequences of decisions during interactive tasks, but feedback often evaluates only the final outcome. The paper argues that this can leave intermediate choices poorly guided and lead to suboptimal policies. QLASS addresses the shortage of intermediate annotations by automatically estimating Q-values step by step.

The method introduces a reasoning tree and process reward modeling to create guidance for individual interactions. Its Q-guided generation strategy uses these intermediate evaluations during inference, helping the agent select steps with attention to their longer-term value. The important shift is to provide useful feedback throughout an agent’s trajectory, where decisions affect what becomes possible later.

Experiments report significant performance improvements on complex interactive agent tasks. QLASS also retains strong performance with almost half the annotated data, indicating efficiency under the evaluated limited-supervision conditions. Qualitative analysis provides additional evidence of more effective decisions. Together, the findings support automatically generated stepwise guidance as a way to improve agent inference when direct intermediate supervision is scarce.
icml-2025-qlass-boosting-language-agent-.tldr: QLASS automatically estimates stepwise action values to guide language agents toward better long-term decisions during inference.

paragraphs: The paper seeks a more explicit way to represent quantum states learned from measurement data. Neural representations can predict state properties while offering little insight into how to reconstruct a state experimentally. Here, the representation is a surrogate state-preparation circuit, connecting learned information to a concrete sequence of circuit operations.

The authors build a reinforcement learning agent with a Transformer architecture and a local fidelity reward. It uses measurements from only a few neighboring qubits to learn circuits for estimating properties of target states. They also theoretically analyze the global fidelity achievable when the agent obtains a good local approximation, examining the relationship between local agreement and overall state similarity.

Experiments demonstrate learning for several state families with up to 100 qubits, including shallow Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial circuit states, Ising-evolved states, and many-body ground states. The learned circuit representations also support Hamiltonian learning through a simple linear model. These results show that explicit circuit representations can serve both state characterization and a downstream learning task.
icml-2025-reinforced-learning-explicit-c.tldr: A reinforcement learning agent turns local quantum measurements into explicit surrogate preparation circuits for state-property estimation.

paragraphs: Reward-Guided Speculative Decoding combines a lightweight draft language model with a more powerful target model to reduce reasoning costs. Its key choice is to permit controlled bias toward outputs with higher reward. This changes the objective from strictly preserving an unbiased decoding process to managing the trade-off between computation and output quality.

A process reward model evaluates intermediate generation steps and helps decide when to invoke the target model. The system can therefore allocate the expensive model’s work according to the assessed quality of the reasoning in progress. The authors theoretically establish an optimal resource-performance balance for a threshold-based mixture strategy.

Evaluations include challenging reasoning benchmarks and Olympiad-level tasks. The authors report up to 4.4 times fewer FLOPs than decoding only with the target model, alongside better average accuracy than a parallel decoding method, with reported gains up to 3.5. These are separate comparisons. Together, they support reward-guided routing as a practical way to spend inference computation more selectively.
icml-2025-reward-guided-speculative-deco.tldr: Reward-guided speculative decoding uses intermediate rewards to decide when a stronger model is needed, improving reasoning efficiency.

paragraphs: Gaussian processes become expensive on large datasets because their inference involves large kernel matrices. Kronecker structure can accelerate these operations, but a common construction requires product kernels evaluated on a complete Cartesian grid. Missing observations break that directly visible structure, creating a difficulty for data such as incomplete time series.

The paper retains a structured latent matrix and expresses the kernel matrix for observed values as its projection. In this formulation, missing entries need not erase the underlying computational structure. The authors combine this representation with iterative linear system solvers and pathwise conditioning to perform inference for exact Gaussian processes using fewer resources than standard iterative methods.

Experiments cover real-world datasets with up to five million examples in robotics, automated machine learning, and climate applications. The method outperforms state-of-the-art sparse and variational Gaussian processes in those evaluations. Its contribution is a way to use latent matrix structure despite incomplete observations, expanding the practical reach of exact Gaussian process modeling in the studied settings.
icml-2025-scalable-gaussian-processes-wi.tldr: Latent Kronecker structure enables resource-efficient exact Gaussian process inference when missing observations disrupt a complete grid.

paragraphs: This paper examines how to reuse an existing dense language model when building a mixture-of-experts model. Reusing a smaller model, called upcycling, can reduce the need to start training from scratch. Mixture-of-experts models provide another route to computational efficiency, making their combination an appealing subject for studying training budgets.

Through extensive experiments, the authors derive empirical scaling laws relating performance to dataset size and model configuration. They identify an interaction between the data used for dense-model training and the data used during upcycling. Although increasing these factors improves performance, their interaction limits the efficiency advantage of upcycling at large computational budgets.

The findings provide guidance for scaling the approach and establish conditions under which upcycling outperforms training from scratch within a budget. The practical message is conditional: reuse can be beneficial, but its value depends on how earlier training, subsequent data, and model configuration fit together. The scaling analysis makes those dependencies part of the budget-allocation decision.
icml-2025-scaling-laws-for-upcycling-mix.tldr: Empirical scaling laws identify when converting dense models into mixture-of-experts models is more efficient than training from scratch.

paragraphs: The paper identifies a semantic problem in adapting three-dimensional human pose estimators at test time. Predictions can become overly smooth and drift toward an average pose, losing the meaning of the observed motion. When body parts are occluded or outside the frame, the adaptation can also lack useful guidance.

The proposed approach introduces a motion prior informed by semantics. It combines video understanding with a structured motion-text space so that predicted motion better follows what the video depicts. It also completes missing two-dimensional poses using motion-text similarity, strengthening the prior’s guidance when the visible pose information is incomplete.

Experiments show improvements over state-of-the-art test-time adaptation methods, including more than a 12% reduction in PA-MPJPE on 3DPW and 3DHP. The results support using motion meaning as an adaptation signal alongside pose information. The two components work toward the same goal: keeping predictions tied to the observed activity even when smoothing or missing body observations would otherwise weaken that connection.
icml-2025-semantics-aware-test-time-adap.tldr: A semantics-aware motion prior and missing-pose completion improve test-time adaptation for three-dimensional human pose estimation.

paragraphs: Forecasting multiple time-varying variables requires learning how those variables relate to one another. Temporal Query Network addresses this through an attention mechanism that combines patterns learned across data with relationships specific to the current input. The paper’s focus is capturing these correlations accurately without requiring a large, expensive forecasting architecture.

Its Temporal Query technique uses periodically shifted learnable vectors as attention queries to represent global relationships among variables. Keys and values come from the raw input, supplying local, sample-level information. TQNet builds on this division of roles with a single attention layer and a lightweight multilayer perceptron.

Across 12 challenging real-world datasets, the authors report more robust multivariate correlations and state-of-the-art forecasting accuracy. They also report efficiency comparable to linear-based methods, including on high-dimensional data. The findings suggest that carefully designing how attention combines global and sample-specific information can deliver strong forecasting performance within a compact model, balancing accuracy with computational cost.
icml-2025-temporal-query-network-for-eff.tldr: TQNet combines learned temporal queries with input-derived attention information for accurate, efficient multivariate forecasting.

paragraphs: Some causal quantities cannot be determined uniquely from observed treatment and control data, leaving an interval of plausible values. Covariates can narrow these partial identification intervals by restricting which probability models fit the observations. Computing the resulting bounds leads to a conditional optimal transport problem, whose additional constraints make it harder than standard optimal transport.

The paper proposes a tight relaxation that converts this problem into standard optimal transport while retaining covariate information. It guarantees narrower partial identification intervals for any value of its penalty parameter. As that penalty increases toward infinity, the relaxation becomes asymptotically exact, providing a connection between the computationally simpler problem and the original conditional formulation.

The authors turn this approach into a data-driven estimator implementable with existing optimal transport packages and analyze its convergence rate. Extensive simulations demonstrate effectiveness and better performance than existing methods. The contribution combines tighter causal bounds with an accessible computational formulation, preserving benefits of covariate adjustment while drawing on established optimization tools.
icml-2025-tightening-causal-bounds-via-c.tldr: A covariate-aware optimal transport relaxation tightens causal identification intervals and approaches the exact conditional solution as its penalty grows.

paragraphs: Many state space models for sequences initialize their dynamics using the HiPPO framework. This paper identifies a mismatch between that framework and noisy observations: HiPPO assumes that the incoming data are noise-free. UnHiPPO extends the theory to include measurement noise and derives an initialization that explicitly accounts for uncertainty.

The authors first interpret HiPPO as a linear stochastic control problem in which data act as a noise-free control signal. They then reformulate the observations as noisy outputs from a latent system. The resulting dynamics infer a posterior over that hidden system from the available data, changing how the model incorporates uncertain measurements into its internal state.

The proposed initialization does not increase runtime, according to the abstract. Experiments show improved resistance to noise during both training and inference. The contribution therefore connects a specific modeling assumption to practical robustness: treating observations as uncertain measurements yields an alternative initialization with better behavior under the evaluated noisy conditions.
icml-2025-unhippo-uncertainty-aware-init.tldr: UnHiPPO incorporates measurement uncertainty into state space model initialization, improving noise resistance without increasing runtime.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks can require expensive operations on matrices whose scale follows the graph. Earlier efficiency approaches sparsify either the graph or network parameters, with limitations in flexibility and precision. Unifews addresses both sources of computation through a joint sparsification technique that unifies graph and weight matrix operations.

The method adapts compression across layers and progressively increases sparsity. It supports several architectures and simplifies operations on the fly. The authors also develop a theoretical framework that views sparsified learning through graph optimization, showing that Unifews approximates the learning objective with bounded error while reducing computational overhead.

Experiments report comparable or better accuracy alongside substantial efficiency gains. These include a 10–20-fold reduction in matrix operations and acceleration of up to 100 times, with evaluations reaching graphs containing a billion edges. The findings connect coordinated sparsification to practical scalability: reducing work in graph processing and learned transformations together can preserve predictive quality in the evaluated settings.
icml-2025-unifews-you-need-fewer-operati.tldr: Unifews jointly sparsifies graph and weight operations to accelerate graph neural networks while maintaining comparable or better accuracy.

paragraphs: ZebraLogic evaluates language models on deductive reasoning using logic grid puzzles derived from constraint satisfaction problems. The benchmark varies search-space complexity and includes diverse logical constraints. This creates a controlled setting for examining how a model’s ability to reach correct conclusions changes as the reasoning problem becomes more demanding.

The authors find a substantial decline in accuracy as complexity increases, which they call the curse of complexity. This pattern persists in their evaluations when model size and inference-time computation are increased. The result suggests constraints in current models’ reasoning capabilities, while remaining an empirical finding about the models and scaling approaches studied.

The paper also explores Best-of-N sampling, backtracking, and self-verification prompts as possible ways to improve performance. Its stated contribution is a clearer picture of how reasoning scales across controlled levels of difficulty. The benchmark makes it possible to investigate whether additional resources and generation strategies address the increasing demands of complex deduction.
icml-2025-zebralogic-on-the-scaling-limi.tldr: ZebraLogic finds that language-model accuracy declines sharply on harder logic puzzles, even with larger models and more inference computation.
